discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 0b6e96f80b. `factsOf` now reads only the messages after the newest real prompt (a user message whose `userRunSpan` isn't 0), so an earlier turn's edits or errors no longer drive Verify, Review or Fix; reminders, hook context and steering that core injects mid-run carry `userRunSpan: 0` and stay inside the turn.

Fixed in 0b6e96f80b. `skip` and `unskip` now act on `action.itemId`: the named row is kept out of later sets for the rest of the turn and the next row fills the gap; `unskip` restores it into view from any set served this turn. Ids from another turn, or not in the pool, are refused as stale.

This one doesn't hold. Without `-m`, `git read-tree <tree1> <tree2>` reads both trees into stage 0; it only fails if they share a path, and a checkpoint's tracked tree and its untracked-files parent never do. Repro on git 2.43: read-tree of a tree with `a.ts` and a tree with `new.ts` gives `100644 ... 0 a.ts` and `100644 ... 0 new.ts`, and `write-tree` succeeds. The path is also covered by `sidecar/session-changes.test.ts`, whose checkpoints carry an untracked third parent (including an agent-created `new.ts`), and by a manual run where agent-created untracked files showed up in Last turn and Session.

Fixed in ac405ed: previews compare a symlink by its link text, which is what git stores. Locally the working side uses lstat/readlink; over SSH the index mode (120000) triggers a remote readlink. The explorer itself still follows links on purpose. Real-repo test repoints a committed link and checks old/new are the link texts.

Fixed in 24f543400: the working side of a submodule now reads like git diff: its checked-out HEAD plus '-dirty' when it has uncommitted changes, so an edited-but-uncommitted submodule previews as 'Subproject commit <sha>' -> 'Subproject commit <sha>-dirty' instead of 'No textual changes'. It also checks the path is the submodule's own repository root first, so an uninitialized submodule can't report the superproject's HEAD. Covered in the real-submodule test.

Fixed in b61036cd9: for the index side, treeEntry prefers the stage-0 entry and otherwise our side (stage 2), and the working-copy diff reads it with :2:path, so a conflict previews as ours vs. the working file with markers, which is what git diff shows. If our side deleted the path, git's 'not at stage 0' error is treated as an absent side. Covered by a real-merge-conflict test.

Fixed. An entry whose value is an inline scalar, like `disabled: true` or `disabled: false # note`, is now a single line, so an indented comment after it stays with the author. Block scalars (`|`, `>`) and nested values still take their indented continuation lines with them. Test added for both disabling and re-enabling.
